title: Choose a research method
summary: Choose a method that can answer the decision, and check what the installed tools actually support.
steps: Name the decision, its owner, the relevant population and the uncertainty that matters. Review existing evidence before collecting more.

Use a prototype usability task to observe behavior. Use an implementation A/B/n comparison for differences between working designs on comparable tasks. The current A/B activity assigns one design per session; it is not a paired, within-person comparison.
Use a screenshot first-click test for the initial choice, not end-to-end task completion. Use preference comparisons for stated preference, not proof of better task performance.
Use card sorting to explore grouping and labels; use tree testing to assess findability in a text hierarchy. Neither alone establishes usability of the finished interface.
Use surveys for reported experience and interviews for explanations and context. Reported intention or confidence is not observed completion or comprehension.

Check the installed version before promising a workflow. Servant currently targets Studio 0.3.24 for draft imports; newer public releases may behave differently. The current runner does not provide participant recruitment, automatic clustering or a validated winning-design declaration.
Record alternatives and limits. Moderated sessions, interviews, field work and some accessibility questions need methods outside the unmoderated runner. Plan those with suitable tools and support.
questions: What evidence would change the decision?
Can this method measure the outcome, with this population and access needs?
Which work is supported here, and which needs another approved workflow?
example: To learn whether people understand a waiting status, score their interpretation against a predefined rubric. A click, a preference or a claim of confidence alone does not establish that understanding.
